hook.text: In 1950, Frank McNamara forgot his wallet at a restaurant. That embarrassment created Diners Club.

buildup.text: A card that let you pay later at any participating merchant. Charge now, settle monthly.

discovery.text: Visa and Mastercard turned this into a network. Any merchant, any bank, anywhere in the world.

twist.text: Credit cards make spending painless—literally. Brain scans show less pain than paying with cash.

climax.text: Consumer credit enabled the modern economy. Spending no longer depends on what's in your pocket.

punchline.text: A forgotten wallet invented a trillion-dollar industry.

quiz.question: What inspired the creation of the first credit card?

details.summary: The credit card industry began in 1950 when Diners Club issued the first charge card, followed by the first revolving credit cards from BankAmericard, now Visa, in 1958..
details.whyItMatters: Credit cards changed consumer behavior by making purchases painless and debt invisible. They created a multi-trillion dollar industry where card networks, banks.
takeaways: Diners Club issued the first charge card in 1950 for restaurant payments
BankAmericard, now Visa, introduced the first true revolving credit card in 1958
Interchange fees paid by merchants fund rewards programs and issuer profits

faq.question: How do credit card companies make money?
faq.answer: Through three main streams: interchange fees of 1.5 to 3.5 percent charged to merchants on each transaction, interest charges on consumer balances averaging 20 to 25 percent annually, and annual fees, late fees, and foreign transaction fees. Merchant interchange fees are the largest revenue source.

faq.question: How did credit cards change consumer spending behavior?
faq.answer: Research shows consumers spend 12 to 18 percent more when paying by card versus cash. The psychological pain of payment is reduced when using cards. Revolving credit enables spending beyond current income. Reward programs incentivize card usage over cash, further increasing spending.
